NKJV.1: And Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had gone to Shechem to make him king.
NKJV.2: So it happened, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard it (he was in Egypt, where he had fled from the presence of King Solomon), that Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
NKJV.3: Then they sent for him and called him. And Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
NKJV.4: “Your father made our yoke heavy; now therefore, lighten the burdensome service of your father and his heavy yoke which he put on us, and we will serve you.”
NKJV.5: So he said to them, “Come back to me after three days.” And the people departed.
NKJV.6: Then King Rehoboam consulted the elders who stood before his father Solomon while he still lived, saying, “How do you advise me to answer these people?”
NKJV.7: And they spoke to him, saying, “If you are kind to these people, and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
NKJV.8: But he rejected the advice which the elders had given him, and consulted the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
NKJV.9: And he said to them, “What advice do you give? How should we answer this people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke which your father put on us’?”
NKJV.10: Then the young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, “Thus you should speak to the people who have spoken to you, saying, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you make it lighter on us’—thus you shall say to them: ‘My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s waist!
NKJV.11: And now, whereas my father put a heavy yoke on you, I will add to your yoke; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scourges!’ ”
NKJV.12: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had directed, saying, “Come back to me the third day.”
NKJV.13: Then the king answered them roughly. King Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders,
NKJV.14: and he spoke to them according to the advice of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to it; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scourges!”
NKJV.15: So the king did not listen to the people; for the turn of events was from God, that the LORD might fulfill His word, which He had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
NKJV.16: Now when all Israel saw that the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king, saying: “What share have we in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to your tents, O Israel! Now see to your own house, O David!” So all Israel departed to their tents.
NKJV.17: But Rehoboam reigned over the children of Israel who dwelt in the cities of Judah.
NKJV.18: Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was in charge of revenue; but the children of Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. Therefore King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste to flee to Jerusalem.
NKJV.19: So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.

ESV.1: Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
ESV.2: And as soon as Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it (for he was in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon), then Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
ESV.3: And they sent and called him. And Jeroboam and all Israel came and said to Rehoboam,
ESV.4: “Your father made our yoke heavy. Now therefore lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke on us, and we will serve you.”
ESV.5: He said to them, “Come to me again in three days.” So the people went away.
ESV.6: Then King Rehoboam took counsel with the old men,  who had stood before Solomon his father while he was yet alive, saying, “How do you advise me to answer this people?”
ESV.7: And they said to him, “If you will be good to this people and please them and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever.”
ESV.8: But he abandoned the counsel that the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him.
ESV.9: And he said to them, “What do you advise that we answer this people who have said to me, ‘Lighten the yoke that your father put on us’?”
ESV.10: And the young men who had grown up with him said to him, “Thus shall you speak to the people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you lighten it for us’; thus shall you say to them, ‘My little finger is thicker than my father's thighs.
ESV.11: And now, whereas my father laid on you a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.’”
ESV.12: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king said, “Come to me again the third day.”
ESV.13: And the king answered them harshly; and forsaking the counsel of the old men,
ESV.14: King Rehoboam spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.”
ESV.15: So the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn of affairs brought about by God that the LORD might fulfill his word, which he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
ESV.16: And when all Israel saw that the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king, “What portion have we in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Each of you to your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, David.” So all Israel went to their tents.
ESV.17: But Rehoboam reigned over the people of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah.
ESV.18: Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram,  who was taskmaster over the forced labor, and the people of Israel stoned him to death with stones. And King Rehoboam quickly mounted his chariot to flee to Jerusalem.
ESV.19: So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.

AMP.1: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
AMP.2: When Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard about the new king (for he was in Egypt, where he had fled from the presence of King Solomon), Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
AMP.3: And the people sent messengers and summoned him. So when Jeroboam and all Israel came, they spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
AMP.4: "Your father [King Solomon] made our yoke hard (heavy, difficult); so now lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke which he put on us, and we will serve you."
AMP.5: Rehoboam replied, "Come back to me again in three days." So the people departed.
AMP.6: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon [as advisers] while he was alive, asking, "What advice do you give me in answer to these people?"
AMP.7: They answered him, saying, "If you are kind to these people and please them and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever."
AMP.8: But the king rejected the advice which the elders gave him, and consulted with the young men who grew up with him and served him [as advisers].
AMP.9: He asked them, "What advice do you give to us regarding the answer to these people, who have spoken to me, saying, 'Lighten the yoke which your father put on us'?"
AMP.10: The young men who grew up with him told him, "Tell the people who said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you make it lighter for us': 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins!
AMP.11: Now my father loaded you with a heavy yoke, but I will add [more weight] to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions (extremely painful scourges).'"
AMP.12: So on the third day Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam just as the king had directed, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
AMP.13: The king answered them harshly, for King Rehoboam rejected the counsel of the elders.
AMP.14: He spoke to them in accordance with the advice of the young men, saying, "My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to it; my father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions."
AMP.15: So the king did not listen to the people, for the turn of events was from God that the LORD might fulfill His word, which He had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
AMP.16:
When all Israel saw that the king did not listen and pay attention to them, the people answered him,
"What portion do we have in David?
We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse.
Every man to your tents, O Israel;
Now, [Rehoboam, descendant of] David, see to your own house."
So all Israel went to their tents.
AMP.17: But as for the Israelites who lived in Judah's cities, Rehoboam ruled over them.
AMP.18: Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was over the forced labor, and the Israelites stoned him and he died. And King Rehoboam hurried to mount his [royal] chariot to escape to Jerusalem.
AMP.19: And Israel has rebelled against the house of David to this day.

CSB17.1: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, <sup>ⓙ</sup> for all Israel had gone to Shechem to make him king.
CSB17.2: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about it — for he was in Egypt where he had fled from King Solomon’s presence — Jeroboam returned from Egypt. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.3: So they summoned him. Then Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam:
CSB17.4: “Your father made our yoke harsh. Therefore, lighten your father’s harsh service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”
CSB17.5: Rehoboam replied, “Return to me in three days.” So the people left.
CSB17.6: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had attended his father Solomon when he was alive, asking, “How do you advise me to respond to this people?”
CSB17.7: They replied, “If you will be kind to this people and please them by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
CSB17.8: But he rejected the advice of the elders who had advised him, and he consulted with the young men who had grown up with him, the ones attending him.
CSB17.9: He asked them, “What message do you advise we send back to this people who said to me, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
CSB17.10: Then the young men who had grown up with him told him, “This is what you should say to the people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you, make it lighter on us! ’ This is what you should say to them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
CSB17.11: Now therefore, my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, but I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, but I, with barbed whips.’” <sup>[1]</sup>
CSB17.12: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had ordered, saying, “Return to me on the third day.”
CSB17.13: Then the king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam rejected the elders’ advice
CSB17.14: and spoke to them according to the young men’s advice, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓛ</sup> but I will add to it; my father disciplined you with whips, but I, with barbed whips.”
CSB17.15: The king did not listen to the people because the turn of events came from God, <sup>ⓜ</sup> in order that the LORD might carry out his word that he had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.16:
When ⓐ all Israel saw [3] ⓑ that the king had not listened to them, the people answered the king: What portion do we have in David?
We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse.
Israel, each to your tent;
David, look after your own house now!
So all Israel went to their tents.
CSB17.17: But as for the Israelites living in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
CSB17.18: Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, <sup>[4]</sup> <sup>ⓒ</sup> who was in charge of the forced labor, but the Israelites stoned him to death. However, King Rehoboam managed to get into his chariot to flee to Jerusalem.
CSB17.19: Israel is in rebellion against the house of David until today.

NLT.1: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel had gathered to make him king.
NLT.2: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of this, he returned from Egypt, for he had fled to Egypt to escape from King Solomon.
NLT.3: The leaders of Israel summoned him, and Jeroboam and all Israel went to speak with Rehoboam.
NLT.4: “Your father was a hard master,” they said. “Lighten the harsh labor demands and heavy taxes that your father imposed on us. Then we will be your loyal subjects.”
NLT.5: Rehoboam replied, “Come back in three days for my answer.” So the people went away.
NLT.6: Then King Rehoboam discussed the matter with the older men who had counseled his father, Solomon. “What is your advice?” he asked. “How should I answer these people?”
NLT.7: The older counselors replied, “If you are good to these people and do your best to please them and give them a favorable answer, they will always be your loyal subjects.”
NLT.8: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the older men and instead asked the opinion of the young men who had grown up with him and were now his advisers.
NLT.9: “What is your advice?” he asked them. “How should I answer these people who want me to lighten the burdens imposed by my father?”
NLT.10: The young men replied, “This is what you should tell those complainers who want a lighter burden: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
NLT.11: Yes, my father laid heavy burdens on you, but I’m going to make them even heavier! My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions!’”
NLT.12: Three days later Jeroboam and all the people returned to hear Rehoboam’s decision, just as the king had ordered.
NLT.13: But Rehoboam spoke harshly to them, for he rejected the advice of the older counselors
NLT.14: and followed the counsel of his younger advisers. He told the people, “My father laid heavy burdens on you, but I’m going to make them even heavier! My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions!”
NLT.15: So the king paid no attention to the people. This turn of events was the will of God, for it fulfilled the LORD’s message to Jeroboam son of Nebat through the prophet Ahijah from Shiloh.
NLT.16:
When all Israel realized that the king had refused to listen to them, they responded, “Down with the dynasty of David!
We have no interest in the son of Jesse.
Back to your homes, O Israel!
Look out for your own house, O David!”
So all the people of Israel returned home.
NLT.17: But Rehoboam continued to rule over the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah.
NLT.18: King Rehoboam sent Adoniram, who was in charge of forced labor, to restore order, but the people of Israel stoned him to death. When this news reached King Rehoboam, he quickly jumped into his chariot and fled to Jerusalem.
NLT.19: And to this day the northern tribes of Israel have refused to be ruled by a descendant of David.

WEB.14: and spoke to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to it. My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.”
WEB.15: So the king didn’t listen to the people; for it was brought about by God, that Yahweh might establish his word, which he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
WEB.16: When all Israel saw that the king didn’t listen to them, the people answered the king, saying, “What portion have we in David? We don’t have an inheritance in the son of Jesse! Every man to your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David.” So all Israel departed to their tents.
WEB.17: But as for the children of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
WEB.18: Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was over the men subject to forced labor; and the children of Israel stoned him to death with stones. King Rehoboam hurried to get himself up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
WEB.19: So Israel rebelled against David’s house to this day.

NET.1: Rehoboam traveled to Shechem, for all Israel had gathered in Shechem to make Rehoboam king.
NET.2: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard the news, he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon. Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
NET.3: They sent for him and Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
NET.4: “Your father made us work too hard! Now if you lighten the demands he made and don’t make us work as hard, we will serve you.”
NET.5: He said to them, “Go away for three days, then return to me.” So the people went away.
NET.6: King Rehoboam consulted with the older advisers who had served his father Solomon when he had been alive. He asked them, “How do you advise me to answer these people?”
NET.7: They said to him, “If you are fair to these people, grant their request, and are cordial to them, they will be your servants from this time forward.”
NET.8: But Rehoboam rejected their advice and consulted the young advisers who served him, with whom he had grown up.
NET.9: He asked them, “How do you advise me to respond to these people who said to me, ‘Lessen the demands your father placed on us’?”
NET.10: The young advisers with whom Rehoboam had grown up said to him, “Say this to these people who have said to you, ‘Your father made us work hard, but now lighten our burden’ — say this to them: ‘I am a lot harsher than my father!
NET.11: My father imposed heavy demands on you; I will make them even heavier. My father punished you with ordinary whips; I will punish you with whips that really sting your flesh.’”
NET.12: Jeroboam and all the people reported to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had ordered when he said, “Return to me on the third day.”
NET.13: The king responded to the people harshly. He rejected the advice of the older men
NET.14: and followed the advice of the younger ones. He said, “My father imposed heavy demands on you; I will make them even heavier. My father punished you with ordinary whips; I will punish you with whips that really sting your flesh.”
NET.15: The king refused to listen to the people, because God was instigating this turn of events so that he might bring to pass the prophetic announcement he had made through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
NET.16: When all Israel saw that the king refused to listen to them, the people answered the king, “We have no portion in David — no share in the son of Jesse! Return to your homes, O Israel! Now, look after your own dynasty, O David!” So all Israel returned to their homes.
NET.17: (Rehoboam continued to rule over the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah.)
NET.18: King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, the supervisor of the work crews, out after them, but the Israelites stoned him to death. King Rehoboam managed to jump into his chariot and escape to Jerusalem.
NET.19: So Israel has been in rebellion against the Davidic dynasty to this very day.

MSG.1: Rehoboam traveled to Shechem where all Israel had gathered to inaugurate him as king.
MSG.2: Jeroboam was then in Egypt, where he had taken asylum from King Solomon; when he got the report of Solomon's death, he came back.
MSG.3: Summoned by Israel, Jeroboam and all Israel went to Rehoboam and said,
MSG.4: "Your father made life hard for us—worked our fingers to the bone. Give us a break; lighten up on us and we'll willingly serve you."
MSG.5: "Give me," said Rehoboam, "three days to think it over; then come back." So the people left.
MSG.6: King Rehoboam talked it over with the elders who had advised his father when he was alive: "What's your counsel? How do you suggest that I answer the people?"
MSG.7: They said, "If you will be a servant to this people, be considerate of their needs and respond with compassion, work things out with them, they'll end up doing anything for you."
MSG.8: But he rejected the counsel of the elders and asked the young men he'd grown up with who were now currying his favor,
MSG.9: "What do you think? What should I say to these people who are saying, 'Give us a break from your father's harsh ways—lighten up on us'?"
MSG.10: The young turks he'd grown up with said, "These people who complain, 'Your father was too hard on us; lighten up'—well, tell them this: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.
MSG.11: If you think life under my father was hard, you haven't seen the half of it. My father thrashed you with whips; I'll beat you bloody with chains!' "
MSG.12: Three days later Jeroboam and the people showed up, just as Rehoboam had directed when he said, "Give me three days to think it over; then come back."
MSG.13: The king's answer was harsh and rude. He spurned the counsel of the elders
MSG.14: and went with the advice of the younger set: "If you think life under my father was hard, you haven't seen the half of it: my father thrashed you with whips; I'll beat you bloody with chains!"
MSG.15: Rehoboam turned a deaf ear to the people. God was behind all this, confirming the message that he had given to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah of Shiloh.
MSG.16:
When all Israel realized that the king hadn't listened to a word they'd said, they stood up to him and said,
Get lost, David!
We've had it with you, son of Jesse!
Let's get out of here, Israel, and fast!
From now on, David, mind your own business.
And with that they left.
MSG.17: Rehoboam continued to rule only those who lived in the towns of Judah.
MSG.18: When King Rehoboam next sent out Adoniram, head of the workforce, the Israelites ganged up on him, pelted him with stones, and killed him. King Rehoboam jumped in his chariot and escaped to Jerusalem as fast as he could.
MSG.19: Israel has been in rebellion against the Davidic dynasty ever since.

NIV.1:
Israel Rebels Against Rehoboam
Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all the Israelites had gone there to make him king.
NIV.2: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard this (he was in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon), he returned from Egypt.
NIV.3: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and all Israel went to Rehoboam and said to him:
NIV.4: “Your father put a heavy yoke on us, but now lighten the harsh labor and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”
NIV.5: Rehoboam answered, “Come back to me in three days.” So the people went away.
NIV.6: Then King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How would you advise me to answer these people?” he asked.
NIV.7: They replied, “If you will be kind to these people and please them and give them a favorable answer, they will always be your servants.”
NIV.8: But Rehoboam rejected the advice the elders gave him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and were serving him.
NIV.9: He asked them, “What is your advice? How should we answer these people who say to me, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
NIV.10: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “Tell the people who have said to you, ‘Your father put a heavy yoke on us, but make our yoke lighter’—tell them, ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist.
NIV.11: My father laid on you a heavy yoke; I will make it even heavier. My father scourged you with whips; I will scourge you with scorpions.’”
NIV.12: Three days later Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, as the king had said, “Come back to me in three days.”
NIV.13: The king answered them harshly. Rejecting the advice of the elders,
NIV.14: he followed the advice of the young men and said, “My father made your yoke heavy; I will make it even heavier. My father scourged you with whips; I will scourge you with scorpions.”
NIV.15: So the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events was from God, to fulfill the word the Lord had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite.
NIV.16:
When all Israel saw that the king refused to listen to them, they answered the king:
“What share do we have in David,
what part in Jesse’s son?
To your tents, O Israel!
Look after your own house, O David!”
So all the Israelites went home.
NIV.17: But as for the Israelites who were living in the towns of Judah, Rehoboam still ruled over them.
NIV.18: King Rehoboam sent out Adoniram, who was in charge of forced labor, but the Israelites stoned him to death. King Rehoboam, however, managed to get into his chariot and escape to Jerusalem.
NIV.19: So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
